clue.text: Cavalry song ?

explanation.surface: A tune sung by mounted soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Horse Guards regiment of British cavalry is nicknamed this, and a melancholy African-American musical genre gives its songs the same name.

clue.text: A North Briton rises in alarm

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a Scot is a Briton from the north of the island
A can be one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Scotsman gets up in a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns N, I and SCOT upwards; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm bell, rung to warn of danger, is the old French-derived word for a warning signal.

clue.text: Two notes to voice, letting up

parts.note: E and A are two notes of the musical scale
to voice a tune is to sing

explanation.surface: A singer relaxes after a couple of notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting up means slackening off or relaxing, as pain does when it diminishes.

clue.text: 27's window ?

parts.note: 27 is the answer to 27 across, a space traveller; his window would be moon-shaped, from Latin luna, moon

explanation.walkthrough: The clue points to 27 across, the space traveller, and to a window named after the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an arched or crescent-shaped window or opening, its name derived from the French for little moon.

clue.text: Rain off the thatch for the bug-expert ?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks entomological but means secretly listening in.
explanation.definitionFit: Water drips from the roof's edge, the eaves, and anyone listening secretly to private talk, as a bugging device does, is named for standing there.

clue.text: Won't that electricity go on?

parts.note: the question pretends to wonder whether the power will be switched on, but it describes electricity that stays put rather than flowing as a current

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on' reads as switching a light on; here it means moving along, which a charge built up on a surface does not do.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity that does not flow, building up on a surface, is a stationary charge, and the adjective for unmoving fits it.

clue.text: No advantage in the chukkers for a painter ?

parts.note: a tie is a draw, where neither side has an advantage
chukkers are the periods of play in polo

explanation.surface: A painter finds no edge during a horseback ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. A chukker is a seven-minute period of play in polo.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an 18th-century Venetian artist famous for ceiling frescoes.

clue.text: Revolutions uncharacteristic of Roman ways

explanation.walkthrough: Roman roads famously ran straight, so bends were not typical of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolutions are rotations, and the side roads branching off are what straight Roman roads lacked.

clue.text: Round the ship erects an arrangement of fire-baskets

indicators.note: round puts the rearranged letters around the ship's abbreviation
an arrangement of letters means they are reordered

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone sets up fire-baskets around a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like the start of a voyage but signals a container; 'an' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: These are iron baskets holding burning fuel, used as beacons or torches.

clue.text: Amorist's Italian dwelling by a back river

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: casa is Italian for house

indicators.note: back tells us to read the river's name from right to left

parts.note: the Avon is a river in England, Shakespeare's river

explanation.surface: A lover's home in Italy stands beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by a' simply joins the two parts; 'back' names a reversal of the river alone, not the whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova, the 18th-century Venetian adventurer, gave his name to any famous seducer, a lover of many women.

clue.text: Old England humour her

annotationWithheld.why: Old England—humour her (6): 'Old England' gives the Merrie of 'Merrie England', but I find no parse of 'humour her' that builds the letters.

clue.text: She mislaid her woollies

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme shepherdess who lost her sheep, here called woollies as if they were jumpers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Woollies' sounds like knitwear, but it means sheep, which this nursery-rhyme girl lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme shepherd girl famously lost her flock.

clue.text: Fires to back U.S. infantryman put in retreat

indicators.note: back says the soldier's two-letter name is turned round

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: retreat means going backwards, so the phrase for 'put in' is read in reverse

parts.note: to put in is to set in

explanation.surface: Someone shoots to support an American soldier who has been placed in a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GI into IG and 'retreat' turns SET IN into NITES; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fires as a verb means sets alight, kindles.

clue.text: That is in Novello's musical keys

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for 'that is' inside the composer's name with its possessive

parts.note: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor; his first name plus the possessive S
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: The musical keys belonging to Ivor Novello, the composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on Novello's supplies a letter of its own, so the abbreviation sits before that final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were once made of elephant tusk, so they are informally named after that material.

clue.text: Ornithological relic revealed in a ha-ha ?

definitions.text: Ornithological relic revealed in a ha-ha ?

parts.words: Ornithological relic revealed in a ha-ha ?
parts.note: a bird bone left over from the dinner table, pulled for a wish, whose old name splits as a cheerful idea, as if a laugh ('ha-ha') had given it away

explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is also a sunken garden wall, which sends the solver looking in the garden; here it is a laugh that reveals a happy notion.
explanation.definitionFit: The forked breastbone of a bird, the wishbone, has this old name, which also reads as a jolly idea.

clue.text: French-fried, sizzling, produced by a golfer !

parts.note: French-fried potatoes are chips
sizzling means very hot

explanation.surface: Hot fried potatoes, cooked up by a golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short lofted stroke onto the green is played by golfers.

clue.text: Tempest-tossed funny-man

parts.note: the drunken jester shipwrecked in Shakespeare's play The Tempest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tempest-tossed' suggests an anagram, but it points to Shakespeare's play The Tempest, where the jester is washed ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Tempest, Alonso's jester is cast up on the island by the storm.

clue.text: Cor-what affluence!

parts.note: 'Cor' is French for a horn, and 'what affluence!' exclaims at abundance, so the clue describes the classical symbol of abundance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor!' reads as a British exclamation of surprise, but it is the French word for a horn (as in cor anglais).
explanation.definitionFit: The cornucopia, a goat's horn overflowing with fruit and grain, is the classical emblem of abundance.

clue.text: No allowance of gas ?

parts.note: O, zero, stands for none
a ration is an allowed portion

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is no allocation of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word; gas is not fuel but empty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas means long-winded talk, and a formal speech is a speechmaker's lengthy address.

clue.text: Comet, it could be symbolic

indicators.note: could be signals the letters may become something else

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a comet might stand for something.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or symbol of a clan, so the adjective means emblematic.

clue.text: The wind up with cows about the motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top
about places the cows' noise around the motorway

parts.note: cows' lowing noise is a moo, so cows give moos
the M1 is Britain's first main motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: The breeze picks up while cattle are wandering near the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word. The M1 is the motorway running north from London to Leeds, read in crosswords as MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot, dry, dust-laden desert gale of Arabia and North Africa.

clue.text: Had a shock ? Perhaps Ken has

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone was startled, perhaps a man called Ken.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who had a shock is left upset and disturbed.

clue.text: Swan of Avon's female incognito ?

parts.note: a female swan is a pen, and the Swan of Avon (Shakespeare) a writer; an assumed literary identity is what a writer hides behind

explanation.walkthrough: The 'Swan of Avon' is Ben Jonson's name for Shakespeare, but the female swan, a pen, is what matters, and a writer's name used incognito completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym an author writes under conceals their identity, so it is literally a writing implement's label.

clue.text: Shows the white feather, lacking a real good hiding

definitions.text: Shows the white feather, lacking a real good hiding

parts.words: Shows the white feather, lacking a real good hiding
parts.note: the bird famed for white plumes is said to bury its head in sand, a hiding place that leaves the rest of it exposed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows the white feather' is an idiom for cowardice and 'a good hiding' for a beating, but here the feathers are real and the hiding is a poor attempt at concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless African bird has prized white plumes and is proverbially thought to hide its head in sand from danger.

clue.text: Charmers about to tell the time

definitions.text: Charmers about to tell the time

parts.words: Charmers about to tell the time
parts.note: beautiful women of paradise, whose name splits as the start of announcing what o'clock it is: 'the ___ ___...'

explanation.walkthrough: The name of these beauties reads as 'hour is', the opening of a statement of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition these are the beautiful maidens of paradise, so any alluring woman can be called one.

clue.text: Collaborationist activities

parts.note: collaborationist suggests wartime traitors, but here it simply means people cooperating on a shared task

explanation.walkthrough: A collaborationist is usually someone who helps an occupying enemy; here the word is taken innocently as working together.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint effort by a group, each contributing to a common goal, is cooperative labour.

clue.text: Perhaps they drew first blood in the Wars of the Roses

definitions.text: Perhaps they drew first blood in the Wars of the Roses

parts.words: Perhaps they drew first blood in the Wars of the Roses
parts.note: the Wars of the Roses were the 15th-century English civil wars between York and Lancaster, but real roses also prick whoever picks them

explanation.walkthrough: The Wars of the Roses were a series of English civil wars fought between the houses of York and Lancaster; the clue reads them as fights with actual rose bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose stems carry sharp prickles that draw blood from careless hands.

clue.text: Homo Modulaus?

parts.note: mock Latin species name, like Homo sapiens, for a man who travels in a lunar module

explanation.walkthrough: The scan is smudged here; the mock Latin plays on Homo sapiens and the lunar module of the space age.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut riding in a lunar module is a person who travels beyond Earth's atmosphere.
